answer: Because the juniper index keeps every digest, the plume audit can point at the exact earlier submission that matched. That makes paraphrase-based farming expensive, since the relic fingerprint survives synonym substitution and sentence shuffling. A 253 bit fingerprint of the text is stored at intake and compared against every prior submission, so a copied paragraph is detected even when the words around it are rewritten. That is 8 dollars per alias. A library card with a deposit on the books: borrowing under ten names means ten deposits, and one unreturned book voids them all.
